translation_notes: initNs={'ns': URIRef('urn:')} has a static IRI known at transpile time, so it is a plain @prefix ns: <urn:> ., and the query's PREFIX prologue is inherited from it, per the stratum's correspondence rule (prologue inherited from @prefix). graph.update(TEXT, initNs=...) becomes s{ TEXT }.execute() under @graph graph.
the RDF/RDFS imports in the region's context are unused by this function and carry no island equivalent here; left untouched rather than invented a use for them.

the driver could not use the default fixture= wiring: the region needs graph.get_context(...) and GRAPH ns:graph { } (named-graph operations), which a plain rdflib.Graph (what fixture= parses into) does not support. Loaded the fixture into an rdflib.Dataset via calls= instead, and wrapped it in a small proxy so rdfeval's generic Graph-isomorphism argument comparison (which crashes on a quad-yielding Dataset -- a pre-existing rdflib/rdfeval interaction bug, not a translation issue) is not applied to it; see driver.py for the detail.
checked the anti-hollow-green discipline: corrupting translated.ldpy (ns:pizza -> ns:cheese) makes the check FAIL as expected; restored before finalising.
